article_title: Raising medical students' awareness for the interdependence between oral health and systemic diseases - evaluation of a problem-based learning intervention: an exploratory pilot study.
citation: Pöschel Katharina, Geier Anne-Kathrin, Frese Thomas, Schmalz Gerhard, Schrimpf Anne Marie, Bleckwenn Markus, Ziebolz Dirk, Deutsch Tobias. (2026). Raising medical students’ awareness for the interdependence between oral health and systemic diseases - evaluation of a problem-based learning intervention: an exploratory pilot study. BMC Primary Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12875-026-03323-4
title: PBL case story “A Case for Erna” integrating oral health into the 5th-year geriatrics course
description: A clinical case story embedded in the mandatory Leipzig PBL course “Medicine of Aging and the Aging Person”, in which an older patient newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes develops severe periodontitis and later a heart attack. The article states that “The pathology of periodontitis, its diagnostics and therapy, and its possible effects on systemic inflammatory diseases were newly introduced to the students”, alongside oral examination training. Students work in tutor groups of up to nine with a trained tutor over a 90-minute live session plus preparation and follow-up.
requirements: Tutors who completed a one-week medical education course and mandatory preparation sessions
A detailed teaching guide and a catalog of learning objectives
constraints: Delivered as live online sessions in summer 2021 due to COVID-19 restrictions
The two-day case format was judged possibly too short to address all topics with due intensity
target_learning_goals: Confidence in performing oral examinations and identifying at-risk patients
Appreciation of interprofessional collaboration with dentists
examples: One of six clinical cases in the 2021 summer semester PBL course carried the new content, complemented by lectures and practical exercises
key_sources: Pöschel Katharina, Geier Anne-Kathrin, Frese Thomas, Schmalz Gerhard, Schrimpf Anne Marie, Bleckwenn Markus, Ziebolz Dirk, Deutsch Tobias. (2026). Raising medical students’ awareness for the interdependence between oral health and systemic diseases - evaluation of a problem-based learning intervention: an exploratory pilot study. article_title: Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication.
citation: Liu Minling, Mo Xiaocong, Li Tingwei, Dai Huiru, Fang Shuo. (2026). Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1792396
title: The A-SPIRE teaching model: six iterative stages from theoretical understanding to practical creation of tailored health messages
description: The A-SPIRE model is a structured pedagogical framework grounded in experiential learning and constructivist theory, comprising six iterative stages: Anchoring, Searching, Processing, Integrating, Realizing, and Evaluating. It aims to provide "a structured pathway from theoretical understanding to practical creation of tailored health messages." In the evaluated session, the stages moved students from context-setting through information gathering, mind-map organization, planning strategies for three demographic groups, producing a mask-design communication artifact, to multi-source (self, peer, teacher) evaluation.
requirements: Instruction structured around the six stages with time allocations for each phase, pre-class preparation, and post-class reflection questions
constraints: Evaluated in a single elective session with a uniform output format (mask design), which the authors say constrained diversity of creative expression and applicability across varied health communication contexts
target_learning_goals: audience-tailored science and health communication competency
examples: In the evaluated 135-min session, students researched assigned demographic groups, planned strategies, created an oral-health mask design for their audience, shared works in a WeChat group, and received multi-dimensional self, peer, and teacher assessment.
key_sources: Liu Minling, Mo Xiaocong, Li Tingwei, Dai Huiru, Fang Shuo. (2026). Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1792396

article_title: Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication.
citation: Liu Minling, Mo Xiaocong, Li Tingwei, Dai Huiru, Fang Shuo. (2026). Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1792396
title: Dual-track, phased session design pairing teacher and student activities across the six A-SPIRE stages
description: The article's instructional design divides the session into pre-class preparation, in-class A-SPIRE application, and post-class extended learning, with a flowchart aligning teacher activities, the teaching process, and student activities. Each phase has a set duration, e.g., an "Anchoring Phase (10 min)" using film clips, and a "Realizing Phase (45 min)" in which "Student groups created a precision science communication work (mask design) on 'oral health' for their assigned audience," followed by sharing and multi-dimensional evaluation.
requirements: Pre-class questionnaire to assess prior knowledge and readiness; online assessment platform for questionnaires and tests; group work with a shared artifact and multi-source evaluation
constraints: The uniform output format (mask creation) meant suitability of format was not included as an evaluation criterion for this exercise
target_learners: undergraduate medical students in elective courses
target_learning_goals: translating audience-analysis theory into tailored communication artifacts
examples: The 135-minute session allocated 10 min each to Anchoring, Searching, and Processing, 45 min each to Integrating and Realizing, and 15 min to Evaluating.
key_sources: Liu Minling, Mo Xiaocong, Li Tingwei, Dai Huiru, Fang Shuo. (2026). Bridging medical education and public health: a pedagogical model to develop future physicians' capacity in audience-tailored health communication. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1792396

article_title: Objective suturing skill assessment in a hands-on course increases medical students' aspiration to become surgeons.
citation: Onishi Shun, Sugita Koshiro, Murakami Masakazu, Yano Keisuke, Harumatsu Toshio, Tabata Yumiko, Tsuruno Yudai, Kedoin Chihiro, Nagano Ayaka, Kawano Takafumi, Ieiri Satoshi. (2026). Objective suturing skill assessment in a hands-on course increases medical students’ aspiration to become surgeons. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-39306-9
title: A-LAP mini simulator for objective open suturing skill assessment
description: The A-LAP mini (Kyoto Kagaku Co., Ltd.) is a box-trainer simulator "originally designed for endoscopic surgery training" that was used under direct vision to evaluate open suturing. Each participant performed three single-ligature sutures scored on five items: "procedure time, outline area, aperture area, needle count with firmness, and leak pressure", each rated on a 5-point scale with a maximum total of 25 points. The removable suturing sheet allows evaluation comparable to laparoscopic suturing.
requirements: Removable suturing sheet that can be attached to the evaluation device
Scoring on five items each rated on a 5-point scale
constraints: Originally developed for laparoscopic training; used under direct vision in this study
examples: In the study, the median total score was 21 (range 19–22) and median time was 4.8 minutes (4.1–5.7).

article_title: Addressing Culturally Based Hidden Bias and RacisM (A-CHARM) Using Simulation Experiences, Nik's Story: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
citation: Salami Oluwabukola, Wong Josephine Pui-Hing, Sawhney Monakshi, Li Jenny S., Patterson Michaela, Gumapac Nathaniel P., Sau Crystal, Akbari Ali. (2024). Addressing Culturally Based Hidden Bias and RacisM (A-CHARM) Using Simulation Experiences, Nik's Story: A Quasi-Experimental Study. The Canadian Journal of Nursing Research. https://doi.org/10.1177/08445621241253124
title: A-CHARM project: five open-access virtual simulation experiences on racism and hidden bias
description: The A-CHARM (Addressing Culturally based Hidden bias and RacisM) nursing project produced a didactic presentation plus five virtual simulation experiences. "Our team created 5 virtual simulation experiences as part of the A-CHARM project (1. Nik's story, 2. Christian's story, 3. Sophie's story, 4. Yasmin's story, 5. Da-eun's story)." Each scenario depicts navigating an inappropriate or racist comment in a clinical setting using one of four published frameworks, with learning outcomes and reflective questions. "The A-CHARM virtual simulation experiences are available as an open access resource on the CAN-Sim website... or through e-CAMPUS Ontario."
requirements: Developed with both nursing students and faculty involved in development and filming, following CAN-Sim and INACSL standards
constraints: At the time of this study only Nik's story had been tested; the other four simulations' usability and effectiveness had not been examined
target_learning_goals: cultural competence, cultural awareness, and cultural safety in encounters involving racism and culturally based hidden bias
examples: Nik's story was the A-CHARM simulation used in this study because its scenario matched the participants' final clinical practicum context
key_sources: Salami Oluwabukola, Wong Josephine Pui-Hing, Sawhney Monakshi, Li Jenny S., Patterson Michaela, Gumapac Nathaniel P., Sau Crystal, Akbari Ali. (2024). Addressing Culturally Based Hidden Bias and RacisM (A-CHARM) Using Simulation Experiences, Nik's Story: A Quasi-Experimental Study. article_title: Learning Introductory Biology: Students' Concept-Building Approaches Predict Transfer on Biology Exams.
citation: McDaniel Mark A., Cahill Michael J., Frey Regina F., Limeri Lisa B., Lemons Paula P. (2022). Learning Introductory Biology: Students' Concept-Building Approaches Predict Transfer on Biology Exams. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.21-12-0335
title: Construct exams with both a priori designed retention and transfer items to assess deep conceptual understanding
description: The article recommends building summative assessments that deliberately include both retention items (echoing taught material) and transfer items (requiring application of principles to novel situations), with item classification decided before administration. Instructors rated every item on the four-category McDaniel et al. rubric and revised questions until each exam contained at least five strong category 3/4 transfer candidates. This a priori design allowed the study to detect that learner groups identical on retention items diverged sharply on transfer items.
requirements: Instructor collaboration and independent rating of items against the retention/transfer rubric, with iteration until agreement and at least five strong transfer candidates per exam
constraints: Category 2 items that fell definitively in neither category were excluded from analyses; three problematic items were dropped post-administration
target_learning_goals: assessing deep conceptual understanding and transfer rather than memorization
examples: Course instructors worked with an author to rate and revise exam items using the McDaniel et al. (2018) rubric before administering each of four midterms
key_sources: McDaniel Mark A., Cahill Michael J., Frey Regina F., Limeri Lisa B., Lemons Paula P. (2022). Learning Introductory Biology: Students' Concept-Building Approaches Predict Transfer on Biology Exams. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.21-12-0335
